sections.h2: Which Warren County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Two elected offices split the work. The Warren County Auditor values property and administers credits, and the Warren County Treasurer sends the bills and takes payment. The auditor's office is at 406 Justice Drive in Lebanon, and its real estate department answers at 513-695-1235.

The auditor's real estate page says the office maintains records on about 91,400 parcels, covering ownership, legal description, property address, building description, appraised value and the transfer history that feeds the tax list. The treasurer posts rate sheets for every year from 2004 through 2025, so a seller can look up how a parcel's levies have moved.

A third body, the Board of Revision, hears value complaints. It has three members: the auditor, the treasurer and the president of the board of commissioners.

sections.h2: How does Warren County value a house for tax?
sections.html:
The auditor appraises each parcel at its estimated fair market value, then taxes 35 percent of that figure, as the office's appraisal page explains under Revised Code Chapter 5713. Every parcel gets a site visit in a general reappraisal at least once every six years, and a triennial update adjusts values in the third year between those cycles, usually by percentage changes drawn from local sales.

New construction and changes in use are valued every year. The tax lien date is January 1, so ownership and use on that day fix the bill payable the following year.

The auditor's own FAQ says most increases follow the state-required reappraisal, and that without new construction or new levies, bills tend to stay close to the same level between updates. A school levy passed by voters in a district raises bills for the parcels inside it, which is why two similar homes in different school districts can pay different amounts.

sections.h2: When are Warren County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Ohio real estate tax is billed in two halves. For tax year 2025 the treasurer's page printed February 25, 2026 for the first half and August 12, 2026 for the second. The August date was an extension the Tax Commissioner approved after House Bill 186's inflation cap credit delayed the second-half bills, and the treasurer asked owners to wait for the bill rather than send an estimate.

The treasurer takes payment online through myWarrenCountyOhio, by phone at 513-496-2931 or at the office from 7:30 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays. Three forms are posted on the page: an Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties, a Military Extension Application and a Notice of Possible Tax Adjustment.

The penalty rule comes from Revised Code 323.121. A ten percent penalty attaches to an unpaid half after its due date, and if the full amount is paid within ten days, half of that penalty is waived. Interest accrues on delinquent taxes at the rate set under section 5703.47.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Warren County property value?
sections.html:
File a complaint with the Board of Revision on form DTE 1. The auditor's page sets the window from January 1 through March 31 of the following tax year, and the form must be signed in front of a notary by the owner or an attorney.

The board rules on total fair market value of land and buildings. It does not lower tax dollars or rates. The burden of proof sits with the owner, and failing to meet it can leave the value unchanged or even raise it. The board gives at least ten days' notice of the hearing, which is recorded, and mails or emails a decision letter to every party.

  • Strong evidence includes a recent sale below the auditor's value, a recent fee appraisal and proof of damage that lowers the market value.
  • The board may also ask for purchase or lease agreements, closing statements, construction costs, rent rolls or income and expense statements.
  • Bring supporting papers before the hearing date instead of at the hearing.

sections.h2: What tax breaks does Warren County offer homeowners?
sections.html:
The auditor administers the programs below. Each requires you to own and occupy the home as your principal residence, and only one Ohio home can qualify.

Warren County auditor filing rules for homeowner credits and appeals
ProgramWho qualifiesForm and filing time
Homestead ExemptionAge 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or a surviving spouse aged 59 or older of a past participantDTE 105A, received by December 31
Owner-Occupied CreditHomeowner living in the property on January 1DTE 105C, filed on or before December 31
Board of Revision complaintAny owner disputing the market valueDTE 1, filed January 1 to March 31

For the 2026 tax year the homestead page printed an income limit of $41,000, measured by 2025 Ohio adjusted gross income. An applicant who misses the income test can try again the next year, when the state may raise the limit. Disability claims also need a Certificate of Disability (DTE 105E) or another accepted certification.

sections.h2: What is charged when a Warren County home is sold?
sections.html:
The auditor's transfer page prints a mandatory conveyance fee of $1.00 per thousand dollars of the price, a county transfer tax of $2.00 per thousand and a $0.50 fee per parcel. Fees are paid to the auditor before the deed reaches the recorder.

Ohio's statement of value, described in section 319.202, asks the seller whether the current or prior year's tax is being reduced under 323.152, the homestead and owner-occupied credit statute. If it is, the parties sign a sworn paper estimating the reduction and confirming they accounted for it. A similar statement covers farmland valued under CAUV, which can carry a recoupment charge when the use changes.

The statement also tells the buyer how to claim the owner-occupied reduction, and the buyer must notify the auditor if the home later stops qualifying. When the sale involves residential rental property, the auditor endorses the deed with a reminder that the new owner must file the rental registration information.

sections.h2: What should a Warren County seller with back taxes do?
sections.html:
Call the treasurer's office before listing and get a payoff figure that includes penalties and interest. Ask for the figure in writing so the title company can use it at closing. The Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties on the treasurer's page is the route to ask for relief on penalties.

The county also runs forfeited land sales, and the auditor's home page announced one for November 9, 2026. Ask the treasurer or auditor how a delinquent parcel moves toward that kind of sale, and settle the balance early.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Warren County, Ohio?
faqs.a: The Warren County Treasurer does. The auditor sets the value, and the treasurer bills, collects and posts rate sheets. Payment options include myWarrenCountyOhio, and phone at 513-496-2931.

faqs.q: What percent of market value does Warren County tax?
faqs.a: Thirty-five percent. The auditor's appraisal page states that the common level of assessment in Ohio is 35 percent of appraised value, so the taxable value of a parcel is 35 percent of fair market value.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to challenge a Warren County valuation?
faqs.a: March 31. The Board of Revision accepts complaints on form DTE 1 from January 1 through March 31 of the following tax year, and the form has to be signed before a notary.

faqs.q: What income limit applies to the Warren County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: For the 2026 tax year the auditor's page lists $41,000 of 2025 Ohio adjusted gross income. Applicants must be 65 or older, permanently disabled, or a qualifying surviving spouse aged 59 or older, and the form must reach the auditor by December 31.

faqs.q: Can I get Warren County late-payment penalties removed?
faqs.a: You can apply. The treasurer's page posts an Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties and a Military Extension Application. Under Ohio law, paying the full amount within ten days of the due date also cuts the penalty in half.
